from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        x = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        x.move_to(sphere.get_center() + 1.5 * RIGHT)
        minus_x = Dot(color="#0000FF")
        minus_x.move_to(sphere.get_center() + 1.5 * LEFT)
        line = DashedLine(x.get_center(), minus_x.get_center(), color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(label_s2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(x), FadeIn(minus_x))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.play(Flash(x), Flash(minus_x))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Any continuous function maps some antipodal pair.", "These points share identical values.", "Think of temperature on Earth's surface."]
        self.setup_layout("The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements

        globe_label = Text("Earth", font_size=24)
        # Sphere is a 3D surface, not a curve; use get_center() or specific coordinates instead of point_from_proportion

        p2 = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(globe.get_center() + 1.2 * LEFT)
        thermometer = Text("T1 = T2", font_size=24, color=RED)
        formula = MathTex("f(x) = f(-x)", font_size=36)
        
        self.place_at_grid(globe, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(globe_label, "B2")
        self.add(p1, p2)
        self.place_at_grid(thermometer, "E4")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Stolen Necklace Problem", [
            "Thieves must divide a beaded necklace.",
            "Each needs half of every bead type.",
            "This is the discrete necklace problem."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw necklace: 10 red, 10 blue beads in a line
        necklace = VGroup()
        for i in range(20):
            color = RED if i % 2 == 0 else BLUE
            bead = Circle(radius=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=1)
            necklace.add(bead)
        necklace.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(necklace, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(necklace))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Create Thief A and B areas
        thief_a = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=GREEN).set_opacity(0.2)
        thief_b = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=ORANGE).set_opacity(0.2)
        label_a = Text("Thief A", font_size=20).next_to(thief_a, UP)
        label_b = Text("Thief B", font_size=20).next_to(thief_b, UP)
        
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(thief_a, label_a), 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(thief_b, label_b), 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(VGroup(thief_a, thief_b, label_a, label_b)))
        
        # Cuts
        cut1 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=WHITE).move_to(necklace[6].get_right())
        cut2 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=WHITE).move_to(necklace[14].get_right())
        self.play(Create(cut1), Create(cut2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Redistribution animation
        segments = [necklace[:7], necklace[7:15], necklace[15:]]
        
        self.play(
            segments[0].animate.move_to(thief_a.get_center() + LEFT*0.5),
            segments[1].animate.move_to(thief_b.get_center() + RIGHT*0.5),
            segments[2].animate.move_to(thief_a.get_center() + RIGHT*0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We map discrete cuts to a sphere.",
            "Fair division becomes a zero-sum function.",
            "Borsuk-Ulam guarantees an exact fair solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        necklace = Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=YELLOW)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=BLUE)
        point = Dot(color=RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # We map discrete cuts to a sphere.
        self.play(FadeIn(necklace))
        self.wait(1)
        self.place_in_area(necklace, "B2", "B5")
        
        necklace_loop = Arc(radius=0.6, start_angle=0, angle=2*PI, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Transform(necklace, necklace_loop))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fair division becomes a zero-sum function.
        self.place_in_area(sphere, "D2", "E5")
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        
        self.place_at_grid(point, "D3")
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Borsuk-Ulam guarantees an exact fair solution.
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]))
        self.play(point.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Application", [
            "Topology solves complex resource sharing problems.",
            "Fair division is mathematically guaranteed.",
            "Curvature of space ensures perfect fairness."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        pile_a = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)], 
                         *[Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 5)
        pile_b = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)], 
                         *[Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 5)
        
        # Scissors icon as generic shape (simulated)
        scissors = VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=WHITE), Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE)).rotate(PI/4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(pile_a, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(pile_b, 'B5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(pile_a), Create(pile_b))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(scissors, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Flash(scissors))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        fair_text = Text("Fair division is guaranteed", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(fair_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(fair_text))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(*self.mobjects))

outline.topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a sphere (S²) and the idea of 'antipodal points'—two points exactly opposite each other. Visualize this as North and South poles, or any two points x and -x.
sections.example: An animation showing a globe where if you touch a point in Tokyo, the corresponding antipodal point is in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
sections.content: State the core theorem: Any continuous function from an n-sphere to n-dimensional Euclidean space must map at least one pair of antipodal points to the same value. Use a 'Temperature/Pressure' analogy.
sections.example: Visualizing a map of the Earth: At any given time, there must be at least two antipodal points on the surface with the exact same temperature and air pressure.

sections.title: Transition: The Necklace Problem
sections.content: Define the 'Stolen Necklace' problem: Two thieves steal a necklace with k types of beads. How can they cut the necklace to divide the beads fairly (each getting exactly half of each type)? Introduce the concept of a 'discrete' problem mapped to a 'continuous' sphere.
sections.example: A colorful necklace with 10 red beads and 10 blue beads. The goal is to cut the string into segments so that both thieves end up with 5 red and 5 blue beads.

sections.title: The Mathematical Bridge
sections.content: Explain how the discrete necklace arrangement is embedded into a continuous space. By modeling the possible cuts as points on a sphere, the fair distribution becomes a 'zero-sum' function that satisfies the Borsuk-Ulam condition.
sections.example: Animation showing the necklace being stretched into a line, then wrapped around a sphere where the 'cuts' are coordinates on the sphere's surface.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize how a deep topological result provides a concrete algorithmic solution for resource sharing. Emphasize that fair division is mathematically guaranteed by the curvature of space.
sections.example: A final visual of two characters, Alice and Bob, perfectly splitting a 'necklace' of resources using a pair of scissors, representing the Borsuk-Ulam solution.
